authors: F. M. Trier, X. Mao, S. Puthusserypady (DTU)
fit: It's mostly filtering and frequency analysis, which you know from your signal processing courses, plus a standard classifier. The data is public, so you could start in week one.

needs: Laptop only. Public Kumar EEG dataset; optional low-cost EEG headset to collect your own data.
summary: EEG is a cap of electrodes that records the brain's electrical activity through the scalp. People silently imagined letters, numbers or objects, and the computer tried to guess which of the three they imagined. Earlier papers reported very high accuracy, but they tested on the same people they trained on. Tested only on new people, accuracy dropped to about 49% (pure guessing would be 33%).
techniques: Measuring signal strength in frequency bands
Testing only on people the model never saw

terms.meaning: Electrodes on the scalp that record tiny voltages from brain activity.
Brain activity oscillates at typical speeds. Alpha is about 8–14 cycles per second; delta is below 4.
How much of a signal's energy sits in a given frequency range.

summary: In a noisy room, hearing-aid users want to focus on one person. This method uses the hearing aid's microphones to keep sound from one chosen direction and lets the user steer that direction. summary: Some robot touch sensors are a small camera looking at the inside of a soft rubber skin. When the skin presses against something, the camera sees it deform, so touch becomes an image. Training in simulation, then on a real robot

summary: AI models that map floods from satellite images can score well while looking at the wrong things. Radar sees through clouds and ordinary cameras don't, so under clouds a good model should rely on the radar. This paper measures how much each type of satellite input drives each decision and checks that against what experts know. Models with the same accuracy reasoned very differently, and some relied on camera images under thick clouds, a sign they had learned a shortcut.
techniques: Labeling every pixel as flood or not (segmentation)
Measuring how much each input matters (SHAP)
Combining radar and camera satellite images

Labeling each pixel of an image.

title: A vision-based sign language recognition and voice conversion system for inclusive communication

authors: S. Jin, T. Zhou, … J. Kittler
fit: Good if you enjoy the math behind a method. It builds on covariance and linear algebra from your random signals course, and you can start from their code.

needs: GPU for training; public EEG benchmarks (e.g. BCI Competition IV). Strong linear algebra.
summary: Instead of looking at each EEG electrode on its own, many methods look at how pairs of electrodes rise and fall together, summarized in a table called a covariance matrix. These tables have a special mathematical structure, and treating them like ordinary numbers loses information. The authors build a neural network that respects that structure and copes better with very noisy data. Their code is public.
techniques: Neural network that respects the matrices' geometry
Attention (the mechanism used in modern AI models)

title: bacpipe: Making Bioacoustic Deep Learning Models Accessible

authors: J. Yang, E. Hodgson, C. Sun, Z. Erickson, D. J. Weber
fit: It combines everything on your list: body signals, computer vision, robotics and a clear human benefit. The signal processing (filtering, short time windows, smoothing decisions over time) is close to what you did with speech.

summary: EMG measures the electrical signals muscles produce when the brain tells them to move. Even when a spinal-cord injury leaves a hand paralyzed, faint signals still reach the forearm muscles. The team built fabric sleeves with 128 electrodes per arm that pick these up, so a man paralyzed from the neck down could control a home robot just by trying to move his wrists. Over 12 days at home he used it to drink, wipe a table and fetch a drink from another room.
techniques: Turning muscle activity into a heat-map image
Smoothing predictions over time to avoid mistakes
Camera-based object detection and voice commands

terms.meaning: Electrodes on the skin that record the electrical activity of muscles.

Many closely spaced electrodes, giving a detailed map of muscle activity.

authors: M. Roy Chowdhury, S. Sen, Y. Ding
fit: It's a clean example of splitting a hard problem into easier steps, and it's close to your music-genre classifier: features from a signal, then a classifier. All the data is public and it runs on Colab.

summary: A wristband with EMG electrodes records muscle activity while people type. Guessing the exact letter from the muscle signal is hard, but guessing which finger moved is much easier, because each finger uses different muscles. MyoText guesses the finger first, lists the letters that finger usually types, then lets a language model pick the sentence that makes sense. On 30 people from a public Meta dataset, it got about 95 of every 100 letters right.
techniques: Language model to fix the sentence

terms.meaning: Surface EMG: muscle signals recorded with electrodes on the skin rather than needles.
AI trained on text that knows which word sequences are likely.
